issues.claim: The dig-from-above draw is keyed two ways. V04 §3.5.7 (d) (l.1802-1807; IN-V04-3, J-VI.17 H2 from V02 X12) keys it by (the building's lineage, `dig`, the void kind) with 'its key carrying the wing key of a wing V02's mutator adds (V02 §3.9 W6)', so a wing an epoch's MutationPlan step or rung-3 op adds over a void brings a draw of its own. V06 §3.18.1 (2a) (l.2423-2431) keys 'one uniform per (building lineage, dig, void kind)' and states 'a building never draws twice for one kind', and T-V6-34's bar (l.3681) requires 'exactly one draw per (lineage, void kind)'. A building that gains a wing over a void gets a second draw under V04 and none under V06, so the access outcome differs, and T-V6-34 fails a correct V04 build.
issues.required_change: V06 §3.18.1 (2a): key the draw as V04 §3.5.7 (d) does: '(building lineage, `dig`, void kind), its key carrying the wing key of a wing V02's mutator adds (V04 §3.5.7 (d); J-VI.17 H2)'. Replace 'a building never draws twice for one kind' with 'a building draws once per void kind, plus once for each wing V02's mutator adds over a void (a `MutationPlan` step or a rung-3 op, in `scope.basementGrown`)'. Make T-V6-34's last clause read 'exactly one draw per (lineage, void kind, added-wing key)'.

issues.claim: The two units give different outcomes for a void that turns `lost` in an epoch's `afterGrowth` commit. V04 §3.5.7 (g) (5) (l.1861-1864) states without exception that at an epoch a lost cluster's 'households [are] returned to V06's ledger as displaced, cause `void`, and re-housed the same epoch'; V04 §3.10 and V04 §13's V06 row say the same. But (g) runs inside `under.access` at `afterGrowth` 20 (V04 §3.5.7 *With a scope*), and `Foundations.apply`/`ArchVaults.reconcile` in `under.extend` (afterGrowth 10) can collapse a lived cluster's last open path. Both run after `siting` (V06 §3.2 rows 13 and 15). A household put in the ledger there reaches only V06 §3.1 (5)'s `close`, which houses it on the overflow ladder's last rung. V06 instead re-houses such households inside the participant by §4.7's overflow pass: W73, `EpochReport.households.undergroundVacated` ('vacated by … a foundation collapse or a void made lost, and re-housed inside the participant') and V06 §3.18.1 (4), (6) ('never left for close'). V06 §3.18.1 (4) routes only `under.fade`'s decline-step losses through the ledger. The households end up housed differently.
issues.required_change: In V04 §3.5.7 (g) (5) replace 'at an epoch its households returned to V06's ledger as displaced, cause `void`, and re-housed the same epoch' with: 'at an epoch, a cluster turned `lost` at the `decline` step (`under.fade`) returns its households to V06's ledger as displaced, cause `void`, and they are re-housed at `siting` the same epoch. A cluster turned `lost` in an `afterGrowth` participant's commit (`under.extend`'s foundation or arch-vault collapse, `under.access`, `under.undercity`) has its households re-housed inside that participant by §4.7's overflow pass, counted `households.undergroundVacated` and never left for the epoch's `close` (V06 §3.18.1 (4), (6))'. V04 §3.10's access-at-an-epoch bullet and V04 §13's V06 row cite this split.

issues.claim: `hood.fabric`'s epoch draws use two stream-key stages, against V06's one-stage rule. V01 §3.3.6 (l.811) registers the participant with `stage: S9b` but draws its ops 'on `ctx.stream(S7c | S9b, entity)`' (l.830): S7c for item (1), the S7c rule on a district the epoch created, and S9b for item (2). V06 §2.1's `EpochParticipant.stage` is 'the stage its volume names … its draws' stream-key stage and its reads' tag'. V06 §3.16 adds 'participants register the stage their volume names — … `S9b` for `hood.fabric` … — and their draws use that id, their table reads recorded under it (V11 §3.1's Readers, T-V11-1 (b))'. S7c's rule draws (`fabric.select`, V01 §3.12), so the two texts give different stream keys and so different fabrics for an epoch-created district. The `under.*` adapters show V06's convention: they run several V04 stages' functions under the one stage `U-FADE`.
issues.required_change: In V01 §3.3.6 replace 'drawn on `ctx.stream(S7c | S9b, entity)` (`epoch.transform`)' with 'drawn on `ctx.stream(S9b, entity)` (`epoch.transform`; the participant's registered stage, V06 §2.1, V06 §3.16), item (1)'s S7c rule included, its table reads recorded under `S9b`'. Change V01 §3.12's `epoch.transform` line to match.

issues.claim: The primary catacomb complex is chosen with two tie rules. V06 §3.18.2 (3a) (l.2549-2551): 'the complex whose cemetery serves the most burials now, ties by source address'. V04 §3.5.1 (5) (l.1476-1479): 'the complex whose source serves the most burials … ties by rank, so rank 1 at generation — at every derivation; at an epoch, V06's derived primary, the same reading held by its hysteresis'. The two readings are not the same: when served burials tie, V06 picks by address and V04 (at every derivation) by rank. The rank cap (`rankCap` × the primary's extent) then holds a different complex, so the extents differ.
issues.required_change: In V06 §3.18.2 (3a) replace 'ties by source address' with 'ties by rank (V04 §3.5.1 (5): the formation order, rank 1 at generation)', so the epoch's primary is V04's reading held by `catacomb.primaryHysteresis`, as V04 §3.5.1 (5) says.

issues.claim: `interface EvolutionStrategy { id: string; phases: EpochPhase[] }` is declared twice: in base §4.11 (l.7627; agreement.json home: pipeline, 'defined-in-several:V06,pipeline') and in V06 §2.1 (l.400, the same members plus a comment). V06 §2.1's preamble says it holds 'the declarations §4.11 names as this volume's'. §4.11's list (EpochPhase, EpochParticipant, EpochContext, EpochOps, HouseholdLedger, EpochScope, ChurnLedger, EpochStep) does not include EvolutionStrategy.
issues.required_change: Delete V06 §2.1's `interface EvolutionStrategy …` line. Cite §4.11 for it, and move its comment's rule ('one phase per step it implements, in EpochStep order; a step with no phase runs nothing') into V06 §3.1 (4), where it is already stated.

issues.claim: Base §4.11's runner paragraph (l.7638) says 'V06's `'history'` strategy adds the steps `prelude`, `hazards`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `close` and the participant steps'. V06 §2.1, §3.1 (2) and §3.2 say otherwise. `'grow-by-stage'` itself registers `prelude`, which `'history'` reuses and extends with V06 §3.3. `'history'` reuses `demand`, `dossier`, `lapse` and `character`, wraps the base parts of `field`, `siting`, `growth` and `works`, and adds its own phases at `hazards`, `uses`, `departures`, `decline`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `ladder` and `close`. The base list wrongly counts `prelude` as added and omits `uses`, `departures` and `ladder`, steps only the engine implements (V06 §3.2 rows 6, 7, 11).
issues.required_change: In §4.11 replace the clause with: 'V06's `'history'` strategy implements every step of V06 §3.2's order. It reuses the base phases `demand`, `dossier`, `lapse` and `character`, wraps the base parts of `prelude`, `field`, `siting`, `growth` and `works` with its own acts, and adds its own phases at `hazards`, `uses`, `departures`, `decline`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `ladder` and `close` (V06 §3.1 (2)). Participants run at `afterField`, `decline` and `afterGrowth`.'

issues.claim: Base §4.11 *History-first generation* (2) (l.7670-7671) says the replay's epochs 'draw on the ordinary `…/epoch=e` streams (§6.1)'. §6.1's epoch component (l.8621-8623; J-A113.61) keys the replay's coarse epochs r = 1 … R with `0x8000 + r`, a range reserved so that 'no replay draw can equal a live epoch's'. V06 §3.16 (l.2349) reads the §4.11 sentence its own way: 'its epoch component its place in the log'. So the time units give three readings of one key component (VV56-09 raised V06's). The §4.11 wording supports the wrong one, and nothing states which epoch number a live epoch after the creation prefix takes.
issues.required_change: Make §4.11 (2) read: 'they draw on the concerns of the stages each epoch runs, keyed with the replay's epoch component `0x8000 + r` (§6.1 *The history replay*), so the replay is deterministic from the seed and the history and no replay draw equals a live epoch's'. Add a §6.1 clause, under the epoch component, that a live epoch after a replay's creation prefix keys as live epoch e = 1, 2, … (the prefix's epochs counted only in the 0x8000 range).

issues.claim: V07 describes a village way's retirement as a per-year chance; V06's strike pool, which runs it, has none. V07 §3.12 (l.2479-2481) says the street candidate is 'struck at V06 §3.5.2's street rate per year over the epoch's span (`1 − (1 − p)^years`, §4.11 *The clock* (5))'. T-V7-30 (l.3397) and J-V7.98 ('at the street layer's per-year rate') repeat it. V06 §3.5.2, the pool's home, gives each candidate the weight `w = E(x) · rate(layer) · u`. It takes strikes 'in descending w, ties by address, with no second draw (the `u` inside `w` is the pool's only chance), until the district's `fabric` churn cap'. In §4.11's decline table the persistence rate is a weight, not a per-year chance, and the churn caps carry the scaling by years. V07's formula and bar describe different behaviour from the pool that runs the step.
issues.required_change: In V07 §3.12 replace 'struck at V06 §3.5.2's street rate per year over the epoch's span (`1 − (1 − p)^years`, §4.11 *The clock* (5))' with 'struck by V06 §3.5.2's strike pool at the `street` persistence row (its weight `E(x) · rate · u`, under the district's `fabric` churn cap scaled by the epoch's years)'. Apply the same change to T-V7-30's 'struck at V06 §3.5.2's street rate per year over the epoch's span' and to J-V7.98's 'at the street layer's per-year rate'.

issues.claim: V06 contradicts itself, and the counterpart V04 statement, on where a lost void's households go. V06 §3.18.1 (4) routes only `under.fade`'s decline-step `lost` transitions through the ledger ('returning their households as `EpochOps.displaced` (cause `void`), re-housed at `siting`'). W73 and `EpochReport.households.undergroundVacated` say 'a void made lost' is re-homed inside the participant. §3.18.1 (6) covers a dwelling on a collapsed floor but not the other clusters a foundation collapse cuts off. No sentence states the `afterGrowth` case: a cluster turned `lost` by `under.extend`'s foundation or arch-vault collapse, after `siting` (see VAT0-02).
issues.required_change: In V06 §3.18.1 (4) add after the fade-adapter sentence: 'A cluster turned `lost` in an `afterGrowth` participant's commit (`under.extend`'s `Foundations.apply` or `ArchVaults.reconcile`, `under.access`, `under.undercity`) has its dwellings vacated in that batch and its households re-housed inside that participant by the in-participant rule below, never through the ledger (whose pool `siting` has already drained)'. Make W73's and the report comment's wording 'a void made lost after `siting`'.

issues.claim: V02 §13's X23 (l.3717), a hand-off V02 says is 'closed at that destination, which cites this volume', asks V06 to carry 'a solid monument never re-roofed'. No V06 text, and no base text, states this rule. V06 §3.8.2 tier (2)'s repair (`reoccupy` from derelict, 'roof restored', §4.11 `DeclineOp`) and §3.13's `repair` Works apply to every building. The clause was already absent from the archived V06. X23's other clauses are carried: stack order (V06 §3.13 (4)), `rebaseStack` (V06 §3.4 (2)), the deck mutator (V06 §3.19.5 (2)) and the raised-way clearing (V06 §3.19 (7)).
issues.required_change: In V06 §3.8.2 tier (2) and §3.13 (1) add: 'a building with no storeyed wing (V02 §3.15's solid monument, every wing `solid`) takes no roof step: its decay removes no roof it lacks and a repair (`reoccupy` from derelict) adds none — a solid monument is never re-roofed (V02 X23)'.

issues.claim: J-V1.36 (V01 §9, l.3252) still decides 'no epochs in volume 6's first build' for a standalone neighbourhood document. That is a staging statement, implying a later build adds epochs. V06 §1.3 rules a structural absence: 'A standalone neighbourhood document has no clock (V01 J-V1.36): it has no S4–S5 route, so no epoch can grow or shrink it'. V01 §3.10.1 (7)'s body agrees with V06; the decision row contradicts both and reads as deferral wording.
issues.required_change: In J-V1.36 replace 'no epochs in volume 6's first build' with 'no epochs: such a document has no clock (no S4–S5 route), so `advance` and a skeleton's `history` bend (V06 §1.3, V06 §4.1; J-V6.102)'.

issues.claim: V07 §3.12 (l.2269-2271) lists the steps a village epoch runs from the engine: 'every other phase — hazards, demand, the field …, uses, departures, decline, the ladder, the dossier, lapse, character, works — is the engine's'. The list reads as exhaustive but leaves out `prelude`, `fortification`, `terrainWater`, `raisedWays`, `close` and the participant steps. All of these run at a village epoch under V06 §3.1 (4) and §3.2. V07 relies on two of them elsewhere: V07 §3.4 (8) and §3.12 ('the engine's walls step runs over it at every village epoch', item 114) and V07 §3.12's item-110 paragraph ('`raisedWays` step runs its lapse and repair').
issues.required_change: In V07 §3.12 replace the parenthetical enumeration with 'every other step of V06 §3.2's order (V06 §3.1 (4); the participants at their steps) is the engine's', and keep the following clause about the village's `epoch.rows` cell.

issues.claim: V06 gives the ops its phases write the author value `engine`. Examples: 'a `setAttr` of `Way.surface` (author `engine`, cause `rule:field`)' (l.1167, the §2.12 `Way.surface` row l.814, W81 l.345); `Use.strain`'s `setAttr` (l.1732); a raised way's `underuseSince` `setAttr` (l.2791). §7.1's `EditBase.author` is `'user'|'host'|'epoch'|'migration'`, with `'epoch'` the value for an epoch's events. No base type admits `engine`, so these ops carry a value outside the enumeration their EditBase types.
issues.required_change: Write 'author `epoch`' (§7.1's `EditBase.author`) at V06 l.345 (W81), l.814 (§2.12's `Way.surface` row), l.1167 (§3.4 (9)), l.1732 (§3.9's `Use.strain` writes) and l.2791 (§3.19.2 (2)).

issues.claim: V07 writes the `village.pins` participant's pin records with 'author `engine`, cause `rule:village.pins`' (V07 §3.12 *Pins over epochs*, l.2466; V07 §2.6's row 'a village epoch's pins', l.996). §7.1's `EditBase.author` is `'user'|'host'|'epoch'|'migration'` and has no `engine` value (companion of VAT0-13).
issues.required_change: At V07 l.2466 and in V07 §2.6's 'a village epoch's pins' row, write 'author `epoch`' (§7.1's `EditBase.author`).

issues.claim: §7.4's `epoch` lifecycle row (l.10298) and V06 §2.12's row for 'EpochInputs.replay and a replay epoch' (with W84) describe different lifecycles for replay epochs. §7.4's create cell lists `grow`, V06's `advance`, a timeline entry and the port's cadence, but not the history replay's runner, which appends the creation prefix's `epoch` events at generation (§4.11 *History-first generation* (2); V06 §3.20.3). Its undo cell names only 'an epoch that carried a dossier change' as no undo target, not the replay's `creation`-flagged epochs. Its regenerate cell does not say what V06 §3.20.7 states: a Re-derive from S1 or a `generate` re-runs the replay whole from the recipe's history. VDC0-10 covers only the *Replay semantics* paragraph, not this row.
issues.required_change: In §7.4's `epoch` row: add to create 'the history replay's runner at generation, appending the creation prefix's epochs flagged `creation` (§4.11 *History-first generation* (2); V06 §3.20.3)'; add to undo 'a replay epoch of the creation prefix is no undo target (*Replay semantics*)'; add to regenerate 'a replay epoch is re-run only by a Re-derive from S1 or a `generate`, which re-runs the replay whole from the recipe's history (V06 §3.20.7)'.

issues.claim: Shared subject missing from the agreement matrix: the displacement-cause enumeration, `DisplaceCause` (V06 §2.1, l.429: 'fire'|'flood'|'topple'|'contraction'|'works'|'island'|'void'|'clearance'|'redevelopment'). The same union types §2.7's `Household.transit.cause` (file f item 335; VM-R0S-09). V05 (`island`), V04 (`void`) and V02/V06 (`clearance`) write it. Verdict: disagree. V06 §3.20.5 (2) (l.3080) displaces the destruction epoch's households 'into the ledger, cause `destruction`', which neither union contains.
issues.required_change: Add `'destruction'` to V06 §2.1's `DisplaceCause` (the replay's destruction epoch, V06 §3.20.5 (2)). When §2.7's `Household.transit` is written (VM-R0S-09), its `cause` carries the same union, typed as V06 §2.1's `DisplaceCause`.

issues.claim: V06 §3.19 (l.2753) says 'The one row not V11's is `raised.stripMarginM` (1 m), the base's under-deck strip row (§4.3)'. The base declares no such row: `stripMarginM` appears nowhere in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md. V01 §3.14 (l.2131) lists `raised.stripMarginM` (1 m, own) among V01's constants for its under-deck strip rule (V01 §3.17.3 (2)). So V06 gives the constant a home that does not exist and restates its value beside V01's.
issues.required_change: In V06 §3.19 replace 'The one row not V11's is `raised.stripMarginM` (1 m), the base's under-deck strip row (§4.3)' with 'The strip margin is V01 §3.14's `raised.stripMarginM` (V01 §3.17.3 (2)'s under-deck strip)', without the value.

issues.claim: The product's epoch members are declared twice. V06 §2.1 declares `interface ProductDeclEpoch { phases?; participants?; rows?; records? }` 'on §1.1's ProductDecl'; agreement.json gives its home as V06 ('defined'). V07 §2.1's `interface ProductDecl` (l.359-372) declares the same four members again inline, with the same types. V07's `participants` comment also repeats V06 §3.2's participant table (each participant's step, order and stage).
issues.required_change: In V07 §2.1 declare `interface ProductDecl extends ProductDeclEpoch /* V06 §2.1: phases?, participants?, rows?, records? */ { id; rungs; stages; strategies; extraInputs?; tables; version }` and delete the four inline members. State the village's values for them (`siting`/`growth` overrides, the three participants as V06 §3.2's table lists them, the `epoch.rows` cell, `village.records`) once in V07 §3.12, citing V06 §3.2 for steps, orders and stages.

issues.claim: The enceinte part of a buried former fabric is named in a vocabulary the model lacks. V04 §3.5.5 (b) (1) (l.1705-1707): `former` lists 'its ruined ways (traces), its ruined buildings and its ruined enceinte stretches and gates'. `Enceinte.condition` has no `ruined` value, and a tower or gate carries no state of its own (§2.7, file f item 575). The caller, V06 §3.20.5 (2), (4), names the fabric otherwise: for a destruction, every run `breached`; for a decline, 'its dismantled enceinte stretches'. So it is not stated which wall runs (breached, dismantled or both) become V04's wall bands.
issues.required_change: In V04 §3.5.5 (b) (1) replace 'its ruined ways (traces), its ruined buildings and its ruined enceinte stretches and gates' with 'the former fabric V06 §3.20.5 (4) defines — its ruined buildings, its ways retired or effaced to traces, and its enceinte runs in the condition V06 §3.20.5 lists, with the towers and gates drawn on them'.

issues.claim: V06 §3.20.5 (4) (l.3098) defines a district's former fabric as 'its ruined buildings, its ways effaced to traces, its dismantled enceinte stretches and ruined gates'. A gate has no state of its own: it 'draw[s] by its run's `condition`' (§2.7, file f item 575; V06 §2.8's `absorbWall` comment). So 'ruined gates' names a state the model does not hold. V06 also does not state which runs a destruction epoch's buried fabric contributes: §3.20.5 (2) leaves them `breached`.
issues.required_change: In V06 §3.20.5 (4) replace 'its dismantled enceinte stretches and ruined gates' with 'its enceinte runs whose condition is `dismantled` — and, for a destruction's fabric, the runs §3.20.5 (2) left `breached` — with the towers and gates drawn on them (a tower or a gate carries no state, file f item 575)'.
